sections.skill: Locate constraint boundaries as graph intersections

branch.new_demand: Connect the boundary values of constraints to intersections of graphs.
branch.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the optimal and boundary values found algebraically are read from graph intersections.

questions.skill: Locate constraint boundaries as graph intersections
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A garden has width W and area y = W(30 - W) ft². How do the graphs of y = W(30 - W) and y = 200 show that the widths with area at least 200 ft² are 10 ≤ W ≤ 20?
questions.prompt_markup: A garden has width W and area y = W(30 - W) ft². How do the graphs of y = W(30 - W) and y = 200 show that the widths with area at least 200 ft² are 10 ≤ W ≤ 20?

choices.text: The line y = 200 meets the parabola only at its vertex, W = 15, so 15 ft is the only width.
The parabola crosses the W-axis at W = 10 and W = 20, so those are the boundary widths.
The parabola is below the line y = 200 between W = 10 and W = 20, and above it outside.
The graphs intersect at W = 10 and W = 20, and the parabola is on or above the line y = 200 between them.

questions.correct_answer: The graphs intersect at W = 10 and W = 20, and the parabola is on or above the line y = 200 between them.
questions.grading_note: Viable W are where the area graph is at or above 200. The others use the zeros (0 and 30), reverse the region, or misplace the intersections.

questions.prompt: A garden of width W ft has area A = W(30 - W) ft² (0 < W < 30). On axes with W horizontal and area vertical, the parabola y = W(30 - W) and the line y = 200 are drawn. Why do the widths where the parabola is on or above the line give the viable widths for an area of at least 200 ft²?
questions.prompt_markup: A garden of width W ft has area A = W(30 - W) ft² (0 < W < 30). On axes with W horizontal and area vertical, the parabola y = W(30 - W) and the line y = 200 are drawn. Why do the widths where the parabola is on or above the line give the viable widths for an area of at least 200 ft²?

choices.text: At each such W, the height of the parabola is the area W(30 - W), and it is at least 200.
At each such W, the parabola is below 200, so the area is small enough.
At each such W, the width W is at least 200.
At each such W, the area equals exactly 200.

questions.correct_answer: At each such W, the height of the parabola is the area W(30 - W), and it is at least 200.
questions.grading_note: Points on the parabola have height equal to the area. The others confuse "at least" with "equal", reverse the region, or read the wrong axis.
